subtitle: Lesson 19 · System Design for Data Engineers

code:
Consistency (C)         -- every read sees the latest write
Availability (A)        -- every request gets a response
Partition tolerance (P) -- keeps working when nodes can't talk
caption: Only really claims something DURING a partition.

eyebrow: P isn't optional -- so it's really C vs. A
code:
During a partition, a node can:
  Refuse to answer --> consistent, not available (CP)
  Answer anyway     --> available, maybe stale (AP)
caption: A partition will happen. P was never the choice.

eyebrow: CP and AP, already in this chapter's stack
code:
CP-leaning:  single-writer OLTP, synchronous replication
             (Lesson 4) -- errors rather than show bad data
AP-leaning:  a serving-layer cache (Lesson 16) -- serves
             slightly stale data rather than error
caption: Lesson 21's fraud case study leans AP on purpose.
